Field notebook: a small file transfer
Revision: second

Purpose
This notebook is a readable sample file for the transfer example. It describes
an imaginary workshop, its shared tools, and the plan for a quiet afternoon.
The second revision keeps most of these notes and changes only a few facts.

The room
Morning light reaches the long table through three windows. A shelf beside the
door holds paper, pencils, measuring tape, and a box of clean cloths. Everyone
returns borrowed equipment to the shelf before leaving for the day.

The workbench
The bench has enough space for two people to work without moving each other's
materials. A blue tray holds small parts. Larger pieces rest on a cork mat so
they cannot scratch the surface when someone turns a project around.

The garden
A narrow path leads from the workshop to a sheltered garden. The first bed
contains herbs, the second contains flowers, and the last now holds six new
seedlings. A watering can stands under the tap beside the wooden gate.

The reading corner
Two chairs face a low bookcase. The books cover local plants, practical repairs,
simple recipes, and maps of nearby walking routes. A visitor can leave a note
inside the green folder to suggest a book for the next community collection.

The afternoon plan
At three o'clock the group will sort the spare parts and label the storage boxes.
After that, everyone will check the garden tools and repair the loose handle
on the small rake. The final task is to sweep the floor around the workbench.

The noticeboard
A paper calendar lists the next three open afternoons. Beside it, a hand-drawn
map shows the bicycle stands and the sheltered entrance. Visitors should use
the side door when the main room is being cleaned or rearranged.

The kitchen shelf
Tea, coffee, and a jar of ginger biscuits are available during breaks. Each person
washes their own cup and leaves it upside down on the drying rack. The kettle
stays clear of the sink so water cannot splash onto its electrical connection.

The repair log
Completed repairs go into a dated notebook. Each entry explains the original
problem, the parts used, and any checks performed before returning the item.
Unfinished repairs remain on the marked shelf with a short note about next steps.

Closing time
Before leaving, the last two people check the windows and switch off the lights.
They make sure the workbench is clear and the garden gate is closed. The room
should be ready for the next group without anyone needing to move stored work.

Transfer note
This second revision can use the first revision as its shared base. The server
reconstructs these new bytes and verifies their checksum before storing the file.
The delta contains the base identity and compressed changes, not the base bytes.
